summary.oneLiner: Manufacturer of winding and conductivity products (enameled wires, copper/aluminium conductors, strips) for power, electrical and industrial applications, ranked among the top 5 manufacturers by installed capacity in India.
summary.business: The Company manufactures winding and conductivity products including Enameled Wires, Enameled Copper Rectangular Strips, Paper Insulated Copper Conductors, Copper Busbar and Bare Copper Conductors, Specialised Winding Wires, PV Ribbon and Aluminum Paper Covered Strips. Its products are used in applications such as energy generation & transmission, electrical systems, electric motors, clean energy systems, electric mobility and railways, serving over 318 customers domestically and internationally.

related.name: ALCU Industries Private Limited
related.note: Hosts the Proposed Project — new manufacturing unit at Narsanda, Taluka Nadiad, Gujarat, adding 18,000 MTPA capacity

currentContext.expansion: The Company proposes to increase installed capacity from 19,680 MT per annum to 37,680 MT per annum by installing additional 18,000 MTPA at a new manufacturing unit ("Proposed Project") at Narsanda, Taluka Nadiad, Gujarat, 15 kms from its existing operating facilities, under wholly owned subsidiary ALCU Industries Private Limited. Through the Proposed Project, the Company intends to add new products including Copper Foils, Copper Components, Continuously Transposed Copper Conductors, PV Round Ribbon, Solar Cables, Multi Paper Covered Copper Conductors, Enameled Aluminium Winding Wires, and …

one-line thesis: Vidya Wires achieved 24.2% revenue growth and margin expansion in FY26 by successfully commissioning its ALCU subsidiary, which introduced high-margin specialized products for EV and renewables; the company now enters FY27 with 36,000 MT capacity and a clear path to margin uplift through product mix shift, making it a structural beneficiary of India’s grid and energy transition capex.
financial scorecard: revenue: +24.2% YoY; EBITDA: +35 bps margin to 4.66%; PAT: ₹576.1M (rptd); order book: not disclosed; net debt: reduced by ₹100Cr via IPO proceeds repayment; one-offs: ALCU ramp-up costs not fully absorbed in FY26, no accounting distortions noted
guidance: revenue growth: strong volume growth expected; margin: improvement expected from higher-value product mix; order inflow: aligned with ALCU capacity ramp-up; capex/commissioning: full 36,000 MT capacity by Diwali FY26, no further capex announced
segment / subsidiary detail: Power & transmission: 51%; Renewable & EV: 7%; General engineering: 13%; Electricals: 27%; Consumer durables: 3%
growth verticals / optionality: ALCU facility enables entry into PV round ribbon, CTC, copper foils, and aluminium conductors; export target of 25% (currently 12%); land available for future capacity expansion
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improved 35 bps to 4.66% due to back-to-back hedging; new products (aluminium, CTC, PV ribbon) carry higher EBITDA/ton than traditional copper wires; aluminum processing adds 3.5x value-add vs copper
capex / expansion: ₹100Cr of IPO proceeds used for ALCU capex; total capacity expanded from ~19,000 MT to 36,000 MT; no further capex announced beyond FY26
capital allocation: IPO proceeds prioritized: 1) ALCU capex, 2) ₹100Cr debt repayment; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on organic growth and balance sheet strength
risks & watch-items: logistical delays from Middle East conflict; ocean freight inflation; raw material price volatility (mitigated by hedging); competitive capacity expansion by Precision Wires, Ram Ratna, KSH
management quality / tone: Confident, execution-focused, and disciplined; emphasized phased ramp-up, margin protection, and long-term value creation; avoided giving hard FY27 guidance but signaled strong volume and margin upside
non-obvious takeaways: GST subsidy of 45-50% of ALCU investment over 10 years from Gujarat govt; CTC product launch delayed to Oct FY26; copper foil targeting transformers/switchgear, not semiconductors; 35-40% plant fungibility allows dynamic product mix shift

themes.title: Transformer & grid-component shortage
themes.need: Transformer makers are running flat-out at record order books even as core-capacity ramps land (ATLANTAELE 16k->63k MVA, Q1FY27 record order book INR3,117cr on record INR972cr quarterly inflow, Vadod now PGCIL 400kV-approved with a 765kV tech tie-up in final talks; TARIL toward 75k+ MVA, Q1FY27 UEOB INR6,630cr +26% YoY on a >INR1,000cr single-shot PGCIL Ultra-Mega order, though a Changodar-expansion air-pocket held Q1 revenue to +10%; SHILCTECH adding 220kV) yet the binding constraint is still everything INSIDE a transformer - CRGO core steel, CTC/winding wire (KSHINTL/BHAGYANGR), bushings/insulators (YASHHV; 18-24mo lead, ~95% RIP/OIP imported) and transformer oil (APARINDS); both OEMs are now backward-integrating to own the bottleneck (TARIL's INR900-1,000cr CRGO/CTC/bushing/pressboard programme). Capacity-gated supply is the repeated 'need of the hour' and is driving pricing power now, though both OEMs flagged ~60,000 MVA of new 400kV capacity landing industry-wide in 3-4 months as a 1-year-out overcapacity watch-item (neither sees pricing pressure yet).
themes.driver: PGCIL Ultra-Mega order conversion (TARIL's first >INR1,000cr single-shot award) + Vadod/Changodar capacity ramps; 400kV short-circuit tests and 765kV PGCIL approvals due by Q2FY27-end are the next re-rating triggers; TARIL's Changodar restart (Aug-2026) is the swing quarter for its own growth reacceleration.
